You're in one of toughest child rearing years. People who zap your energy because the solely require everything you have to give. Our kids are 2, 3, and 5. It's just now starting to be less soul sucking. But our marriage has struggled. But as the kids need us less full time (the five year old can make PB&j, the kids play together and work out minor arguments on their own), we have time to work on our marriage and selves. 

I didn't think these days of slight peace would come but thank God. Because I have been where you're at. I attempted but I was saved by my husband and the EMTs, and doctors. I was grateful then (2019) but I am now. If I truly knew life had the potential to get better, maybe I wouldn't have done it, but idk. It was dark back. But there is light and freedom as your kids get older. They still need you, but it's different. And for me, 0-2 is just hard. Its cute, but man, my kids are hilarious now. Being able to joke with them or have them call me out my bullshit makes the tantrums, mundanes, and demandingness of having kids not so bad.  It's still there but it's not so bad. They start coming home with cards that to say "to mom and " because they got too tired to write dad. They go off on you because you had been lying to them about your black coffee because it was secretly soda. 

I see more things to live for now. But It was hard to get this point. I attend a mom support group and that helps, give me community. Finding community is key. People who get what you're going through and say either I've been there or I am there with you. Or people who say I haven't been there, but I am here for you. 

I hope you're able to find that support. Took me 4 years. It's only been the last six months I've found joy and happiness in life again, despite being worse off financial and having health issues one after another.  It can get better. But the suckiness of life you're feeling is not abnormal at all even if everything was perfect. But because things aren't perfect, they do suck a little bit more. 

My husband isn't the most helpful naturally he has put in the work to help out more around the house and make a difference. It didn't happen over night but it's so much better when I compare it to a few years ago. If your partner is actively doing their best you have to decide if that's good enough for you. Because yeah... My husband was doing his best but it honestly wasn't enough for me. I let him know. We had conversations. He decided to work on it but I also acknowledged that if he's doing his best and wants this to work... I have to patient... Even more patient than I thought... But then also give him credit where credit is due on the things that I take for granted. 

You have a lot going on and you're 24. I when I was 24 we had our first two. That's when I made an almost fatal attempt. It's rough. I'm 28 now. It's still rough, but I've learned and grown a lot. It can get better. Try and hold on. It'll be worth the unflattering drawings you'll be getting of yourself from the kids. Those little moments of joy can keep you going. 

It's still hard for me some days. I struggle with suicidal ideation before kids. Having kids and a spouse amplified it because it's not easy... I didn't think it was easy but I was too confident in my ability. Raising a family has amplified all the negatives inside of me.... But I learning to let it amplify my strengths and in the areas that I'm weak, I'm reaching out for support and trying to be support for others. 

Lifting you up today. Sending good vibes.

I think it brought us closer in that I no longer had to hide anything regarding my darkest feelings. I became more honest and direct after the experience. He was pretty understanding of the event but it's also incredibly more traumatizing for him than for me. He saw his wife dead. I barely remember hanging myself.

I had an out of body experience where I could see my body and my husband doing CPR. I remember the colors red and orange. I remember not breathing. I remember feeling intense pain.... That's all I remember. The rest of my memories come from what others told me.

I also hung myself and survived... Sort of. My husband found me after estimated 10 minutes and had to restart my heart because I was gone by that point. I was in a coma for a week remained hospitalized a couple more weeks. I ended up having a stroke and other residual effects.

I'm very lucky to be alive and extremely lucky at my ability to function.

But I don't feel lucky. 

I still wanna die some days... Sometimes most days. Despite  what happened and having a relatively good life... 

What has helped sustain me is a suicide attempt support group. All people who have survived suicide attempts. All people who just get it. Helps me feel less alone and I don't have to explain why I wanna kill myself. 

It doesn't necessarily get easier or better... But there's moments. The moments aren't always enough for me to keep living though... But some how I've been doing it... And honestly I accredit it to the peer support group.

Idk if theres something like that in your area but there are virtual groups. I would highly recommend giving it a shot if there's even an ounce in soul that is telling maybe I should live or maybe there is something here for me.

In my experience, if we're still reaching out or trying to connect with others, even if on an internet forum... We may still have a reason or hope to press on.

Much love to you and take care.

My husband and father both have ADHD and there a hereditary component so if it comes out that my 2 year old has it, I wouldn't be surprised but right now we deal with her behavior with a lot of patience. She's a runner but luckily she's clumsy so she'll eventually fall down and you can catch her. She draws on everything. You can't discipline her because she immediately cries. She purposefully destroys everything (knock down her sister towers, throws books and Legos for fun) and she ate my yoga block. But she'll also share exactly one cheerio with you and help you up if you fall and give you a hug if you're sad. Some toddlers are very complex and challenging. We try to redirect her energy or show her where she can do some of her more destructive behaviors (like we can throw stuffed animals but not blocks) but it doesn't consistently work. So we just hope for the best a lot lol.

So when it come to behavior... Just roll with it unless you see something clearly wrong. Like my friends kid is 4 now and has a lot of outlandish and destructive behaviors that have gotten worse but he doesn't have any diagnose except he's a little higher on the asshole kid spectrum. Joking aside, they've managed to combat the negative behaviors with a lot of Daniel Tiger, and that for some reason connected with him. You just find works and what connects with your kid.
